raw_response:
I farm 10.1 mu, and with only 2 people at home and some off-farm work, I will not spread myself too thin. I will do what I did in the past and what I see working around me in Quzhou: keep most land in the wheat-maize rotation, then leave a smaller piece for cotton. Wheat and maize are the main money and grain crops here, and with well irrigation I can push them a bit without being too risky. I only finished primary school, so I do not make it too complicated. I look at last year, look at what the neighbors used, and then adjust a little. If fertilizer feels a bit high, I can still accept that, because losing yield hurts more than wasting a little fertilizer. For wheat, I will put the stronger rate on the better land because that crop starts the whole year. For maize after wheat, I will keep a hybrid and feed it enough nitrogen so it does not go hungry in summer. For cotton, I will not plant too much because it takes more watching and more pesticide, but I will still keep some because I know how to manage it and it can still bring cash if I stay on top of insects. I will use rotary tillage where I need a clean seedbed, and for summer maize after wheat I will save labor and time with no-tillage. That way I can manage the whole farm with the people I have and not spend money in the wrong place.
